# AINA §03 ONE-CALL TECHNICAL BRIEF — EISA Four-Gate Verdict Machine & Strict AST Parser

Nav: PrevBrief=https://blayneaina.com/02/brief.txt | NextBrief=https://blayneaina.com/04/brief.txt | Site=https://blayneaina.com/ | Repo=https://github.com/SquadForge/blayne.aina | Contact=me@blayneaina.com
Executive Summary: Problem: Entity resolution needs rich comparison structure, but raw contacts, companies, and products should not be sent to external AI providers. | Proves: The production EISA Four-Gate machine validates bounded acts over sealed evidence; Semantic Switch is an experimental alpha structure-preservation research module. | Scope: Use the deterministic EISA core for judgment boundaries and evaluate Semantic Switch only against its declared synthetic-test scope.

- Introduction & Thesis [Part 1/6]: # EISA Four-Gate Verdict Machine & Strict AST Parser The production EISA core determines which bounded acts earn constitutional standing; Semantic Switch is an experimental alpha module for structure-preserving entity-resolution research. By Blayne Aina · Principal Systems…
- One Constitution, Two Proof Lanes [Part 1/6]: EISA applies the same rule to two very different proposal classes: The recognition spine is ev_ evidence → eisacase_ sealed case → bounded EISA_ACT_V1 acts → Four-Gate recognition → recognized artifact → immutable eisa_ Room submission.
- 1. Strict Representation Before Judgment [Part 1/6]: Subtopics: Gate 1 begins with strict::parse; The exact ten-key act envelope; Record-relative RFC 6901 pointers; The profile bounds — A grammar cannot govern a transition if two parsers can assign different meanings to the same bytes. EISA does not deserialize submissions through an ordinary last-key-wins JSON map. — Spec/Table: version: Exactly EISA_ACT_V1 | stage: A declared stage whose family admits the opcode: Fracture or Forge | actor: Must match the authenticated caller, case-insensitively | opcode: One of the seven closed opcodes | operands: An object with exactly the opcode's declared keys | evidenceRefs: At most 16 strings naming Room-issued ev_ handles; layout relations require exactly… — Key Rules/Claims: visit_map checks whether each incoming key already exists and rejects duplicates. | visit_f64 refuses non-finite numbers. | de.end() rejects trailing non-whitespace matter after the root value.
- 2. The Closed Grammar: Seven Opcodes, Four Layers [Part 1/6]: The opcode set is closed. New semantics cannot be introduced by sending a persuasive string. Dependencies point downward. Layer 0 observations feed Layer 1 pairs; Layer 1 pairs feed Layer 2 closure; Layers 1 and 2 support the Layer 3 partition. — Spec/Table: 0; Opcode: BindEvidenceTag; Stage: Fracture; Exact operand keys: id, tag, coordinates; Constitutional role: Compare values at two distinct sealed-record coordinates using one positive or counter tag | 0; Opcode: RequestHumanReview; Stage: Fracture; Exact operand keys: id, reason, members; Constitutional role: Emit lawful non-operative review matter over at least one sealed record | 0;…
- 3. The Evidence Alphabet: 17 Tags and 12 Comparators [Part 2/6]: Subtopics: The 47 registered fault classes — EISA's tags are not natural-language hints. Each positive or counter tag binds to one deterministic comparator. The two inferential tags are reserved for transitive composition and are refused in BindEvidenceTag. — Spec/Table: 1; Evidence tag: PHONE_STRONG; Class: Positive; Comparator and exact predicate: DigitsEqual: both digit strings have at least seven digits and are identical | 2; Evidence tag: PHONE_ONE_DIGIT_VARIANCE; Class: Positive; Comparator and exact predicate: DigitsOneSubstitution: equal-length digit strings, Hamming distance exactly one | 3; Evidence tag: PHONE_MULTI_DIGIT_VARIANCE; Class: Positive;…
- 4. Sealed Cases: Two Substrates, One Artifact Identity [Part 2/6]: Subtopics: File cases; Passage cases — An act may point only into a sealed case. EISA creates eisacase_ by hashing the Room name, a NUL separator, and the case's RFC 8785 JCS record digest. The artifactHash carried by every act is that record digest; the Room-qualified case ID is the graph address. — Key Rules/Claims: prepares and validates the citation for the caller and task; | refuses handles from another Room or unrevealed collaborative-pass findings; | loads and reverifies the canonical view and live source; | cuts the exact Unicode-scalar passage using the handle's selector; | refuses textless gaps, empty selections, and…
- 5. The Four-Gate Verdict Machine [Part 2/6]: Subtopics: Counterevidence is submission-complete; Transitive closure is a path proof, not a slogan; Partition verification is global across the admitted submission; Consensus identity removes narrative, not responsibility — Each act ends in one consequence class: A malformed whole submission is inadmissible. A recognized submission reports decision: partition, review, relation, or none; it does not acquire a blanket database-execution verdict. — Spec/Table: 1. Syntax and stage isolation; What the recognizer establishes: Strict JSON, exact keys, closed symbols, authenticated actor, unique IDs, bounded sizes, one act family, matching artifactHash; What it refuses to let the proposal do: Smuggle duplicate fields, foreign opcodes, mixed stages, self-declared actors, or unbounded matter | 2. — Key Rules/Claims: operative — a recognized act with a consensus identity. | lawful_non_operative — a valid review request, which creates no operative identity claim. | anti_knowledge — a valid rejection of other matter. | typed_fault — preserved residue with a fault code and no standing.
- Exhibit A — A Valid Contact Submission [Part 3/6]: The following synthetic submission binds two email relationships, asserts a pair, and proposes a complete partition over three sealed records. artifactHash is the case's bare digest. Values are resolved from the sealed case, not trusted from the prose.
- Exhibit B — `counterevidence_suppressed` [Part 3/6]: Suppose the same submission also admitted act_bind_counter_03, binding DOMAIN_ROOT_MISMATCH on the pair, but act_dup_101_102 omitted it from counter. Its recognized-act report entry is: The refusal is not a score penalty. It is the absence of standing for that pair.
- 6. Proof Lane A: Spatial Relations Without Visual Guesswork [Part 3/6]: Subtopics: From PDF operators to integer evidence; The CONNECTS proof; Branch labels enter relation identity — A flowchart can have perfect OCR and still produce a false graph. Recognizing the words inside two boxes does not establish which arrow connects them, which direction the arrow points, whether the tip touches a node or an enclosing frame, or whether “Yes” and “No” label the same… — Key Rules/Claims: Provenance. All three records come from one Room, view digest, source revision, parser digest, and page. Each record's committed LayoutFact.node is exactly the node its evidence handle cites.
- Exhibit C — An Operative Layout Relation [Part 3/6]: This is the layout portion of a synthetic recognized-act report. The frame fields are observations in the current report shape, not an agent-authored layout_proof object.
- Exhibit D — Two Distinct Partition Failures [Part 3/6]: The first splits records already proven equivalent. The second groups records without proving connectivity. They are different defects and receive different faults.
- 7. Proof Lane B: Semantic Switch First, Then the Entity-Resolution Stack [Part 4/6]: Subtopics: Stage 0 — Semantic Switch: protected computation before external AI; Stage 1 — qBlock: candidate nomination over protected records; Stage 2 — EISA Fracture: identity adjudication with dissent preserved; Stage 3 — EISA Forge: canonical state is a separate decision; Stage 4 — Shield: the baseline moves forward or does not move — Entity resolution adds a different danger: the evidence can contain direct identifiers, and the final merge can be difficult or impossible to reverse through the destination's ordinary product operations. — Spec/Table: SS01: Privacy-first stage responsibility. Semantic Switch transforms native records before provider-exposed qBlock, Fracture, Forge, or Shield computation. Separate stages own identity judgment and destination mutation. | SS02: Whole blocks remain the unit of work. Disjoint IDs, member existence, non-overlap, and in-block edge evidence are checked; no pair-request fragmentation or cross-block… — Key Rules/Claims: every surviving value names its source record and field pointer; | provenance and validity intervals remain inspectable; | declared field quorums and canonical claims decide support; | unsupported values do not win through confidence alone; | a conditional reversal plan records pre-state and post-state commitments…
- 8. From Duplicate Records to Evidence-Linked Relationship Graphs [Part 4/6]: The commercial value is not “AI deduplication” as a slogan. It is a defensible identity substrate on which relationship paths can be inspected. A six-hop query can be a useful exploration horizon. It is not proof of influence, consent, or authority.
- 9. The 2026 Research Landscape: Proposal Quality Is Not Transition Standing [Part 5/6]: The current research supports a hybrid division of labor: models can improve nomination, comparison, and review, while deterministic systems must decide which declared predicates actually hold. The sources do not endorse AINA, and their results need their original scopes. — Spec/Table: Teofili et al., Can we trust LLM Self-Explanations for Entity Resolution? (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01210), June 2026 preprint; What it establishes: Across three LLMs, ten datasets, and multiple prompting strategies, self-explanations were often unstable, weakly faithful, and poorly aligned with counterfactual evidence.
- 10. The Continuous Wire into the Room [Part 5/6]: EISA recognition and Room admission share one path. recognize previews a verdict; submit runs the same recognition logic and records the result. The caller is authenticated, the Room is admitted, the case is loaded and rechecked, and every evidence handle used by a… — Key Rules/Claims: by and native session; | room and optional task; | the case's bare artifactHash; | the complete recognition result; | submission time.
- Exhibit E — The Current Room Ledger Envelope [Part 5/6]: This synthetic show response illustrates the current ledger shape with one operative binding. The per-act report remains inside result. The immutable node is constitutional proof matter for the next boundary. It is not a destination receipt.
- Bring One Bounded Protected-Computation Problem [Part 5/6]: The Semantic Switch & Entity Resolution Challenge applies this constitutional layer to one bounded contact, company, product, or other duplicate-record workflow.
- The Article 03 Claim Card [Part 6/6]: Key Rules/Claims: Mechanism: | Semantic Switch Protected Computation + EISA Constitutional Act Recognition | (native-data minimization, relation-isomorphic fictional records, | qBlock candidates, Fracture, Forge, local exact restoration, Shield, | strict parsing, sealed cases, pointer law, deterministic comparators, | Four-Gate recognition, layout proof, and Room ledger) | Failure it governs: | Native identifiers exposed to external AI computation; | comparison structure destroyed by destructive redaction; | ambiguous or schema-valid model prose becoming authority; | fabricated coordinates and geometry; suppressed counterevidence; | broken transitive claims; incomplete or contradictory…
- Before the Room Can Govern, the Act Must Mean One Thing [Part 6/6]: Return to the three agents voting for a merger. The conventional system can report that the vote was unanimous, the JSON matched a schema, and the judge was 97% confident.
- Frequently Asked Questions [Part 6/6]: Subtopics: Why is JSON Schema or constrained decoding insufficient to govern AI actions?; How does EISA prevent an AI agent from suppressing conflicting evidence?; Does consensusIdentity prove independent agreement?; Why does Semantic Switch run before qBlock?; Is Semantic Switch anonymization?; How does EISA verify flowchart connections without trusting VLM prose?; Does an operative EISA verdict execute the proposed transition? — Constrained decoding establishes shape. It does not resolve record-relative pointers against a sealed case, run deterministic comparators on the values, reject faulted dependencies, force counterevidence into the decision, or prove that a partition is complete, connected, and…
